name: Muthoot Capital Services Ltd
title: Muthoot Capital Services Ltd - 511766 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Vehicle NBFC shifting to retail with co-lending wound down; GNPA cut to 3.94% via ARC sale of INR203 crore at ~45.6% valuation, while AUM guidance of INR4,000-4,200 crore for FY27 is reiterated and pre-tax ROA of 2.5% is far above the ~1% now.

triggers.label: Co-lending wound down, retail 84%
triggers.quote: our own retail portfolio has been considerably increasing. So we have reached 84%, which means our co -lending book has been steadily declining.

triggers.label: FY27 AUM INR4,000-4,200 crore reiterated
triggers.quote: This year, the AUM projections that we had given was around INR4,000 crores to INR4,200 crores, and we will reach those numbers this year.

triggers.label: Q1 2W growth 6% vs industry 14%
triggers.quote: The 2-wheeler industry recorded a 14% year -on-year growth. At Muthoot Capital, we delivered a 6% growth

triggers.label: Pre-tax ROA 1% vs 2.5% target
triggers.quote: As of now, we have reached a stage of 1%, but there are -- now from the next quarter itself

guidance.quote: This year, the AUM projections that we had given was around INR4,000 crores to INR4,200 crores, and we will reach those numbers this year.
yes, we are -- our objective is INR10,000 crores.
we have taken a pretax ROA of around 2.5% for this financial year.
we are expecting the GNPA to be sub -4% only throughout the financial year for the retail segment.
So we are expecting another INR0.40 to INR0.50 down in the upcoming deals as well.
I am expecting at a breakeven level of around 4% of opex, which the company has to operate.

red_flags.quote: So there is no gain from the ARC. It is just that INR83 crores has already been taken a hit over the years.

red_flags.quote: we were only at about 35%, 40% approval rate. So that was being cautious.

Those numbers are available. We can share it on a different call.

summary.headline: Muthoot Capital Q1 FY27: GNPA fell to 3.94% (down ~182 bps YoY) after a ₹203 crore ARC sale; PAT near ₹8 crore.
summary.overview: Management highlighted a CRISIL upgrade to AA minus stable, public deposits crossing ₹100 crore, and a sharp GNPA decline driven by a third ARC sale of ₹203 crore at about 45.6% valuation. Co-lending was wound down to ₹499 crore from roughly ₹1,000 crore a year earlier, with retail AUM rising to ₹2,851 crore. Q1 disbursements were ₹564 crore consolidated (₹535 crore standalone), with PAT near ₹8 crore and PBT near ₹11 crore. Management kept the ₹4,000-4,200 crore FY27 AUM target and ₹10,000 crore FY28-29 ambition, while acknowledging a 2.5% pre-tax ROA target is still far from the current ~1%.

financial_highlights.change: vs 5.81% a year ago (per CFO, retail)
incremental borrowing cost in Q1 at 9%
balance sheet up ~1% QoQ from ₹4,079 crore
standalone ₹535 crore vs ₹508 crore in Q4

segments.name: 2-wheeler
segments.commentary: Still the largest book, with a stated blended yield of 22% and GNPA around 3.5%; the portfolio is shrinking after excluding DA and ARC sales, down ~1% YoY on a stable basis. 2-wheeler industry grew 14% in Q1, against MCSL's 6%.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles and construction equipment
segments.commentary: CV and CE yields are about 17.5%, CV GNPA about 0.36% and CE growth about 75% YoY. CV and used car together grew about 40% YoY.

segments.name: Used car
segments.commentary: Yield 18.6%, GNPA 1.31%; now 8.5% of AUM vs 2% a year ago. Management targets breakeven in FY27 with opex falling from 6-6.5% toward 4% of AUM.

segments.name: Corporate loans
segments.commentary: Book in run-off, down 16% YoY; one corporate account carries ₹15-16 crore of GNPA with collateral now held as asset held for sale, recovery expected in 6-8 months.

segments.name: Dealer channel
segments.commentary: Q1 dealer-channel business ₹465 crore vs ₹421 crore in Q1 FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM target of ₹4,000-4,200 crore reiterated; Q3 (festive season) expected to be the biggest quarter, with disbursements scaled up from end-Q2.
Long-term target of ₹10,000 crore AUM for FY28-29 reiterated; FY28 AUM growth implied at about 150% if FY27 reaches ₹4,000-4,500 crore (analyst's framing, not confirmed by management).
Pre-tax ROA target of about 2.5% for FY27; current pre-tax ROA around 1%; management says impairment cost is not expected to rise much further this year.
Retail GNPA guided below 4% and NNPA below 2% through FY27, with no change to ECL policy or 50% PCR.
Further ₹0.40-0.50 reduction in borrowing cost expected after the CRISIL upgrade; ECL model revision due in about four weeks, with a possible LGD cut from ~50% to 40-42% held back as buffer.
capex_capacity: Approval rate deliberately held at 35-40% of logged cases vs industry 75-80%; management plans to scale disbursements from end-Q2 once an in-house scorecard is live.
Average productivity in car and CV rose to ₹20 lakh+ from ₹13-14 lakh last year, with a target of ₹30-35 lakh.

Branch activation: 25-30% of Muthoot FinCorp's 4,000+ branches generate at least one vehicle loan a month; target 50-60% by year-end. Group entities contribute 15-20% of incremental sourcing, targeted at 40%.
Tech: AI bots handle the entire X-bucket collection, with 55% resolution in the month; QR-code on-spot approvals at dealerships.
Equity raise: 2-3 investors in talks, with meetings expected in Q2; the company is comfortable with leverage up to 6x debt-to-equity.
demand_pricing: Q1 disbursement growth was held back by deliberately low approvals and the wind-down of co-lending, which fell from ~₹120 crore in Q1 FY26 to ₹20 crore in April 2026.
Pricing is moving to risk-based, reviewed weekly with an in-house scorecard in place of quarterly vendor reviews.
Management says competitors in its Tier 2-3 markets price in a similar range, so NII pressure is not expected near term.
ARC pricing: ARC-3 valued at a blended 45.61% (SR investment ~₹81 crore), versus 50-55% in the earlier two ARC deals.

qa_highlights.question: How will the 2-wheeler and retail book be repositioned in FY27-28 to defend margins amid rising funding costs and fintech competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is diversifying into CV, CE and car, which carry lower GNPA (sub-0.5% on existing book), is cutting funding costs through the rating upgrade, and is moving to risk-based pricing with an in-house scorecard. Liability franchise is said to cost about 150 bps less than the average borrowing cost.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ARC transaction details and how do they compare with prior ARC deals?
qa_highlights.answer: The third ARC covered ₹203 crore (₹83 crore write-off pool plus a 600+ DPD GNPA pool of ~₹120 crore) at a blended 46.51% valuation. The first ARC (Sept 2023, ₹235 crore pool) has recovered 75% of its SR; the second (Sept 2024, ~₹100 crore) has recovered 46.71%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the accounting impact of the ARC sale on profit?
qa_highlights.answer: The ₹83 crore write-off pool was fully impaired in prior years. Recoveries of ₹14 crore so far are recognised in this year's P&L with no gain on the sale; 85% of the ₹14 crore is held as SR investment, and the ~₹120 crore pool sold for ₹78 crore against a ₹59 crore provision and ₹60.34 crore book value.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and FY28 AUM targets, and how is the ₹10,000 crore goal progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 AUM target of ₹4,000-4,200 crore is intact; ₹10,000 crore is still the goal for FY28-29. Two-wheeler is to fall to about 30% of the book over three to four years, with car, CV, CE and tractors making up 70%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROA outlook for the used car book, given its 18.6% yield?
qa_highlights.answer: Used car is expected to reach about 1-1.5% ROA, with breakeven targeted in FY27. Impairment cost is about 0.5% against 2-2.5% for two-wheeler, and opex is to fall from 6-6.5% to about 4% of AUM as productivity rises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the group-channel ROA and how is group sourcing performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Group entities contribute 15-20% of incremental sourcing, targeted at 40%. Management says group-sourced business carries lower acquisition costs and somewhat higher ROA than the dealer channel but did not share numbers on this call.

risks_watch: Fresh equity raise is still pending, with meetings expected in Q2 and leverage at 4.88x.
The ECL model revision is due in about four weeks; a possible LGD cut could release provisions but is being held in reserve.
Two-wheeler borrowing mix and rising cost of funds could pressure margins if the rating-driven cost reduction slows.
Retail GNPA of 3.49% excludes one corporate loan; the 3.94% total GNPA depends on that account's recovery through a property sale in 6-8 months.
Management flagged macroeconomic risks (including war) to the FY28-29 AUM target, and the company has not disclosed an ROA plan beyond FY27.
Credit acceptance rates of 35-40% limit growth until the new scorecard is in use.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on asset quality, funding cost and the rating upgrade, but cautious on growth, with approvals deliberately held at 35-40%. Management was more evasive on the pending equity raise and on the group-channel ROA, which it deferred to a later call.
key_quotes: Our GNPA level reduced to 3.94%, representing a decline of about 182 basis points year -on-year.
So overall dip in numbers Y -o-Y is a function of that, but MCSL alone has grown.
But yes, that INR10,000 crore s guidance is still intact.
So the 2 -wheeler used to be our warhorse for a long.

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 AUM of ₹4,000-4,200 crore and a ₹10,000 crore FY28-29 objective, with a 2.5% pre-tax ROA target, but backing is partial: scorecard-led disbursement scale-up from end-Q2, productivity gains and a further ₹0.40-0.50 borrowing-cost cut, with no quantified capacity or order book behind AUM growth, while the current balance sheet AUM is only up ~1% QoQ.
